items.title: Letby trial doctor barred from treating patients was expert witness in another case
items.desc: Prof Peter Hindmarsh played key role in conviction of two Birmingham parents whose son died after diabetes episode A doctor who gave expert evidence that helped to convict Lucy Letby, and who was barred during the trial from treating patients, was then instructed as an expert witness in another prosecution. The Guardian revealed this week that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, during the main trial of Letby, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). The jury, who five months later convicted Letby of the murder of seven babies, were never told. Continue reading...

items.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory. Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. items.title: UK operation wards off risk of cyber-attack on supermarket fridges and freezers
items.desc: News of vulnerability comes after retailers in at least seven European countries hit by cyber-attacks A secret government cybersecurity operation recently warded off the risk of a cyber-attack on fridges and freezers in UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums, it has emerged. An attack would have been similar to those that have caused many millions of euros of damage in continental Europe in recent months. But, while many retailers have now been protected, researchers warned that many more could still be vulnerable. Continue reading...

items.title: Burnham seals trade and youth mobility deals in biggest step towards EU since Brexit
items.desc: Agreements reached on food and drink, emissions and to allow young people to move around continent, but may be derailed over student fees Andy Burnham has taken the biggest step towards deeper ties with the EU since Brexit, sealing deals to ease trade and create a mobility scheme for young people as he declared a “new world” of cooperation between the two sides. At a major summit in Brussels on Friday the EU and UK announced three deals, on food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme, which will allow 100,000 young Britons to live, work, study and travel in the EU, with reciprocal access for Europeans in the UK. Continue reading...

items.title: Voters in four out of five UK parliamentary seats back rejoining EU

The constituency-level modelling across Great Britain found that 512 seats now favoured rejoining, while 73 backed staying out, and 47 were too close to call, in a survey that will boost Andy Burnham’s case for opening the debate on returning to the EU. Continue reading...

items.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
items.desc: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib , during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading...
